subject: high altitude mining town
title: What If You Lived at 5,000 Meters in Half the Oxygen? 50,000 People Do

scenes.text: What if you lived at 5,000 meters, in half the oxygen? 50,000 people do.
La Rinconada, Peru, is the highest permanent town on Earth, a gold mining camp at around 5,100 meters.
Each breath holds about half the oxygen of sea level. Altitude sickness starts at 2,500 meters; this is twice that.
Their bodies answer with red blood cells. Lots of them: 80 percent of the blood, against 40 percent in Lima.
That thick blood carries oxygen, but about one in four residents has chronic mountain sickness.
No running water, no sewer, food trucked up the mountain. They stay for the gold, at the very edge of what a human body can do.

description:
What if you lived at 5,000 meters with half the oxygen? About 50,000 people do in La Rinconada, Peru, a gold-mining town at around 5,100 meters, the highest permanent settlement on Earth.
Residents get roughly half the oxygen pressure of sea level. Their blood adapts until red cells make up about 80 percent of it, against about 40 percent in Lima, yet nearly one in four has chronic mountain sickness (Expedition 5300, CNRS). The town has no running water or sewer system.
What should we run through next?

first_comment: Scientists who went up to study the town said the 80 percent hematocrit was probably the highest value they had ever measured in a human. How high have you ever slept, and what should we run through next?
